label: Early original-phase input of p / a / y
explanation: Fires mostly (94% of mass) in the original input phase, most often at t=0..5 with a peak at t=3. Input token is the strongest single cue: p, a and y have 4-6x lift and together carry about 57% of mass. The strongest activations (near max) are p or a input at t=3-4 after a prefix of the hard-to-recall letters n/x/u/g/i/h. Steps right after those p/a hits (any token, including <DEL>) often show weaker residual activation. It nearly never fires in the copy phase (0.7% rate) and is weak on repeated tokens (in_first=0). Magnitude goes up with an n/x/u/g/i/h prefix and with mid-early position. Precision and recall are both only about 0.5: many p/a/y steps stay below threshold, and many active steps are other tokens whose activation depends on history. Adding history clauses (counts of n/x/u/g/i/h seen) did not lift F1 above about 0.53.
